Makes a frame between each two of the game's: a 30 fps game is shown at 60, and with the PS5 set to 120 Hz a 60 fps game at 120. Adds a little lag and can smear fast motion. Needs V-Sync.

With Frame Generation on, the game's own frames are shown at an even 30 a second and frame generation fills in the rest, for a steady 60. For games that swing between 30 and 60. The game still runs at full speed, but this doesn't make a slow game faster. Leave it off for games that hold 60.
The FPS overlay also shows each frame's times, the display's flips and frame generation's state.
Frames shown for each of the game's: 2x makes one in between, 3x and 4x two or three where the display has the room (a 30 fps game at 120 Hz). More is smoother, with a refresh more lag each.
Steady makes frames only while the game's frame rate is even. Always makes them whenever a frame has the room, even or not.
Stops making frames for a while when they slow the game down.
The made frames show the interpolation's choices in color: gray still, green moved, red and blue edges.
